sections.national_history: Clerical-nationalist and national histories of French Canada before and around the founding of the RHAF.
sections.schools: The Montreal and Laval schools of the 1950s–60s and their debates over the Conquest and Lower Canada.
sections.modernist: The post-1970 generation’s social, economic, urban and women’s history of Quebec, and its syntheses.
sections.quiet_revolution: The origins and meaning of the Quiet Revolution, including the Catholic Action revision moved here from cdn_religion_reform (Q12).
sections.debate_reflection: Historiographical reflection and the 1990s ‘normal society’ debate.
sections.comparative_ideas: Comparative, sociological and intellectual histories at the turn of the century.

records.citation: Paul-André Linteau, “La nouvelle histoire du Québec vue de l’intérieur,” Liberté 147 (1983): 34–47; reprinted in Éric Bédard and Julien Goyette, eds., Parole d’historiens: anthologie des réflexions sur l’histoire du Québec (Montréal: Presses de l’Université de Montréal, 2006), OpenEdition, chap. 35.

verification.checked_against: OpenEdition text of the reprint (source note gives Liberté 147, 1983, pp. 34–47); Crossref DOI for the chapter
verification.note: Read: a generation born about 1945 and trained at Laval and Montréal in the late 1960s wrote ‘une histoire différente’; it concentrated on c. 1850 to the present to understand industrial, urban Quebec; moved from the history of French Canadians to the history of Quebec’s whole population; social history began in Quebec in the 1960s under Annales influence, but the cohort was shaped more by French and Quebec sociologists and American historians; serial sources; Marxism challenged it but few adopted it fully. Linteau stresses a break around 1970.

records.supports: The modernist generation in its own words, including its debts and its distance from the Annales.
